name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Add a rolling 30-day failure-rate window for the top 20% of prompts by usage. This keeps the audit focused on the most impactful prompts without ignoring recent trends. The trade-off is ignoring low-usage prompts that might be failing silently—accept that risk to prioritize high-impact fixes.

name: Gauge
text: The rolling 30-day window still misses the real waste: prompts that fail *silently*—not just in usage, but in user dissatisfaction. A better alternative is a combined metric: usage-weighted failure rate *and* user-reported issues, with a 7-day decay to catch fresh regressions. Settle it by running both for a week and comparing which catches more actual user pain.
